label: Average JD — Vague comp, missing tool versions, unclear reporting line
jd_text:
Embedded Systems Engineer — Hardware/Firmware

Company:
We are a high-tech manufacturing company building next-generation industrial control systems. Our
products are deployed across power, automotive, and industrial automation sectors.

Role Summary:
We are hiring an Embedded Systems Engineer to design and develop firmware and board-level hardware
for our control platforms. You will work closely with the hardware and systems teams to bring new
products from schematic through to production.

Responsibilities:
- Design and develop embedded firmware in C/C++ for ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers
- Design schematics and PCB layouts using Cadence and Altium
- Bring up new boards and debug hardware/firmware integration issues
- Participate in design reviews and contribute to design documentation
- Support manufacturing during production ramp

Required Skills:
- Bachelor's or Master's in Electronics or related field
- Experience with embedded C/C++ firmware development
- Experience with Cadence and Altium for schematic capture and PCB layout
- Familiarity with common lab equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers)
- Understanding of communication protocols (I2C, SPI, UART, CAN)

Preferred:
- Experience with SPICE simulation
- Exposure to functional safety standards

Reporting and Team:
You will be part of the engineering organization and will collaborate with cross-functional teams.

Compensation and Benefits:
Compensation is competitive and includes health insurance and standard benefits. We are committed
to building a diverse and inclusive workplace and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

cached_advisor_report.benchmark_comparison: A solid mid-tier manufacturing JD. Best-in-class postings add explicit salary bands, tool versions, and a named reporting line.

dimension_breakdown.narrative: The posting is reasonably complete overall, though a few areas could be strengthened to bring it closer to best practice.
Tools such as Cadence and Altium are named and protocols like I2C/SPI/UART/CAN are listed, though no versions or proficiency levels are given.
The responsibilities (firmware plus board bring-up plus PCB layout) align reasonably with an experienced embedded engineer profile.
The readability is acceptable and the length feels about right for a role at this level.
An inclusion statement is present, though brief and generic.
Compensation is described only as 'competitive' with no band, which weakens the posting for the Indian manufacturing market.

suggested_additions.suggestion: Add specific version numbers for Cadence and Altium tools used.
suggested_additions.impact: Lets candidates self-assess tooling fit precisely.

suggested_additions.suggestion: Clarify the reporting structure and who the role reports to.
suggested_additions.impact: Reduces ambiguity about seniority and team placement.

suggested_additions.suggestion: Provide a concrete salary band instead of 'competitive'.
suggested_additions.impact: Improves candidate response rate in the India market.

suggested_additions: Specify Cadence and Altium version numbers and the required proficiency level
State the exact reporting line and the team size the engineer will join
Replace 'competitive' with an explicit INR salary band
Add SPICE simulation experience to the required skills rather than preferred
